title: Keep your radiator or baseboard clear
summary: Furniture and curtains in front of a heat source keep the heat from reaching the room.

title: Seal your door with a sweep
summary: Weatherstripping and a door sweep close the gap most exterior doors leak through.

title: Find your drafts
summary: You can't seal a gap you haven't found. A short walkthrough of where heat actually escapes.
question: How do I find where my apartment is actually losing heat?
misconception: If you can't feel a breeze, there's no draft.

title: Understanding your heating system
summary: What kind of heat your rental has, how to tell by looking, and what each kind means for your bill.
question: What kind of heat do I have, and what does that mean for me?
misconception: All heat is the same, so it does not matter which kind the apartment has.

title: Cut your hot water use
summary: Shower length, laundry temperature, and a dripping tap all affect the bill.
impactNote: A tap dripping about once a second can waste more than 3,000 gallons a year; fixing common leaks saves about 10% on the water bill (EPA)

title: Swap in LED bulbs
summary: LEDs use a fraction of the electricity incandescent bulbs do. Keep the originals in a box.
impactNote: LED bulbs use up to 80% less energy than incandescent bulbs (U.S. DOE)

title: Cut phantom load
summary: A power strip you can switch off stops plugged-in devices from drawing power all day.

title: Read your bill
summary: kWh, rate, and what's actually driving your electric bill. Start here.
question: What is actually driving my electric bill?
misconception: The total dollar amount on your bill tells you how much electricity you used.

title: Seal your windows with film
summary: A plastic film kit over a drafty window, on in an hour, off at move-out.

title: Use a space heater safely
summary: A space heater runs on electricity and typically costs more to run than it seems. Safety comes first.
safety: Keep 3 feet of clearance from anything flammable, never leave it unattended, plug it directly into a wall outlet, and buy only a listed/certified unit.

title: Set your thermostat back
summary: Turning the heat down while you are out or asleep typically uses less energy than holding one temperature all day.
impactNote: DOE estimates a programmable thermostat used for setback can save about 10% a year on heating and cooling costs
